name: Laurel Halo
label: Awe
lede: A freeform-radio DJ from Ann Arbor who sang through a Hyperdub debut, went instrumental, scored runways and a documentary, then started her own label and made a piano record that Pitchfork put at No. 26 of 2023.

eras.title: Freeform radio, a show house, a piano bench
eras.text: Laurel Anne Chartow grew up in Ann Arbor on piano, violin and guitar, in a town that also had a freeform college station and Detroit's electronic music next door. Both her parents worked in the auto industry. She took all of it to New York in 2009.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection · Flow State: Laurel Halo interview
years.h: Laurel Anne Chartow is born in Ann Arbor, Michigan
years.p: Wikipedia gives her birth name as Chartow and her hometown as Ann Arbor, where she learned piano, guitar and violin as a kid. Her own website says Detroit.
years.xp:
In a 2011 interview with The Quietus she said she grew up playing "piano, violin and guitar," and that her parents both worked in the auto industry for decades before having to move on as it failed.

She has said she was obsessed with the romantic and impressionist piano composers as a kid, among them Debussy, Ravel, Satie, Rachmaninoff and Shostakovich. Those pianos come back on Atlas, nearly two decades after she left Michigan.

years.src: The Quietus: Metal Confection · Flow State: Laurel Halo interview · Wikipedia: Laurel Halo
years.h: A show on WCBN and a house called Arborvitae
years.p: She hosted a program on the University of Michigan's freeform station WCBN and lived in an Ann Arbor show house called Arborvitae. Wikipedia dates her career to 2006.
years.xp:
The Quietus interview has her calling WCBN "one of the few remaining freeform stations in the country." The first festival she ever went to was the Detroit Electronic Music Festival, which she described as an ear-opening experience.

Her later influences include Warp and 4AD records and a lot of local Michigan music, from Detroit techno to electro and minimal, she told Flow State.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection
years.h: She moves to New York City
years.p: Halo relocated to New York in 2009. Playing with a band and a rehearsal space meant managing everybody's schedules, she told The Quietus, and she began working alone.

eras.title: King Felix goes online
eras.text: A self-released EP with her own voice on it drew offers from several labels, and Halo picked Hippos in Tanks. In a year and a half she had two more EPs, a collaborative record with Daniel Lopatin and a label she had not expected to be noticed by.

q: I was just excited about working with Hippos In Tanks.
years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection
years.h: King Felix EP puts her voice on top of the synths
years.p: Halo's debut EP came out on Hippos in Tanks. She sings on it, which set the expectation for what came next.
years.xp: King Felix was first released online, and multiple labels got in touch afterwards, Halo told The Quietus in 2011. She said she was excited to work with Hippos in Tanks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection
years.h: Hour Logic EP: fewer vocals, same expectations
years.p: Hippos in Tanks released the second EP. Halo said people expect you to do the exact same thing again, and she sang less.

years.h: FRKWYS Vol. 7: a collaboration with Daniel Lopatin
years.p: Halo appears on RVNG Intl.'s FRKWYS series alongside [[Oneohtrix Point Never|9cea062d-d476-447f-98b4-e67e14bfd1e4]]'s Daniel Lopatin and others.

years.h: Demos go to Hyperdub's Steve Goodman
years.p: Halo sent LP demos to [[Kode9|e95a9d7f-fc26-4e56-8032-90cd954deea0]] (Steve Goodman), head of Hyperdub, and got a positive response. Quarantine followed.

eras.title: Hyperdub, and a voice nobody tuned
eras.text: Hyperdub put out her first two albums and an EP in 18 months. Quarantine kept her singing untreated and won a lot of year-end love; Chance of Rain dropped the vocals and went to the floor.

years.src: Wikipedia: Quarantine (Laurel Halo album) · Wikipedia: Laurel Halo
years.h: Quarantine: a debut album with the vocals left dry
years.p: She recorded it at home in Brooklyn between July 2011 and February 2012, with some instruments added in London. She made more than thirty demos and discarded eighteen.
years.xp:
Halo chose not to process her vocals. Per Wikipedia she said there is a "brutal, sensual ugliness in the vocals uncorrected" and that painfully human vocals made sense. She described the themes as contrails, trauma, volatile chemicals and viruses.

The cover adapts Makoto Aida's Harakiri School Girls, which she saw at a Japanese pop art show in New York. The Wire named it its release of the year, and Metacritic has an 80 for it. Tiny Mix Tapes later put it 25th among the decade's best albums.

years.h: She moves to Berlin
years.p: Wikipedia dates her relocation from New York to Berlin to 2013; she has lived between there and, later, Los Angeles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chance of Rain (Laurel Halo album)
years.h: Chance of Rain: nine instrumentals, art by her dad
years.p: Halo produced every track herself. The sleeve is a drawing by her father, Arthur Chartow, from the 1970s.
years.xp:
Wikipedia collects the critics: Metacritic 78, Exclaim! 9/10, Pitchfork 7.4, NME 7. Fact ranked it No. 36 of 2013 and Tiny Mix Tapes placed it 14th.

It is the record where she stops singing and lets jazz-inflected techno and musique concrete take over.

eras.title: Berlin, a hologram pop star, a residency
eras.text: Halo left Hyperdub for one EP, worked with orchestras of unusual kinds, and came back to the label with her broadest record. Then she started writing for film.

years.h: In Situ: a double EP, eight instrumentals, Honest Jon's
years.p: The 35-minute release is her record on the Honest Jon's label. Resident Advisor praised its live-manipulated textures, and Metacritic has it at 73.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · Wikipedia: Atlas (Laurel Halo album)
years.h: Terepa EP with Julia Holter and Rashad Becker
years.p: Halo made the Terepa EP on Other People with [[Rashad Becker|339d8939-7aee-4296-92b6-64b2559666a6]], [[Julia Holter|45610c1f-41a4-44f1-9da6-227510073ffc]] and NH'Koxyen. Becker later mastered Atlas.

years.h: Still Be Here: a show built around Hatsune Miku
years.p: CTM and Transmediale commissioned a soundtrack for the Vocaloid star Hatsune Miku, which premiered at HKW in Berlin.

years.h: Dust: back on Hyperdub with a full band of guests
years.p: Recording began at a two-week EMPAC residency in Troy, New York, in 2015. Eli Keszler, Julia Holter, Michael Salu, Klein and Lafawndah played or sang on it.
years.xp:
Halo took lyrics from concrete poetry, Aram Saroyan and Anne Carson's Sappho translations, then randomized the lines. The lead single, "Jelly," came out April 20, 2017, with vocals by Klein and Lafawndah.

Metacritic has an 84 from 18 reviews. Fact ranked it No. 6 on its 2017 list and Gorilla vs. Bear put it at No. 5.

years.h: Raw Silk Uncut Wood: six ambient pieces with Oliver Coates and Eli Keszler
years.p: It grew out of her work scoring the documentary Possessed. The title comes from Ursula Le Guin's Tao Te Ching translation.
years.xp: It was released on Latency, and announced June 13, 2018 alongside the title track. Pitchfork's Sasha Geffen wrote that it marks a departure from her usual thorny, cerebral electronic compositions. Metacritic has an 84.

years.h: Tru / Opal / The Light Within You with Hodge
years.p: A collaborative EP with Hodge on Livity Sound.

eras.title: Runways, NTS, and her own label
eras.text: Halo spent four years between records scoring fashion shows, mixing a DJ-Kicks and curating at London's MODE. Along the way she launched Awe as a label, a radio show and a way of making records.

years.h: She scores Eckhaus Latta's Fall 2019 show at New York Fashion Week
years.p: The first of several fashion commissions.

years.h: DJ-Kicks on !K7
years.p: Halo's mix for the !K7 series is Vol. 68.

years.h: Possessed score released by the Vinyl Factory
years.p: The soundtrack for the Metahaven and Rob Schroder documentary finally got its own release.

years.h: She walks for Chloe in Paris
years.p: Halo appeared on the Chloe Spring 2021 runway at Paris Fashion Week.

years.cap: Awe w/ Laurel Halo on NTS
years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The FADER: Laurel Halo creates
years.h: Awe starts as a monthly NTS show
years.p: Guests included Kode9 and Mica Levi. The name became her label.
years.xp: The FADER says Atlas is the debut on her own imprint Awe, which is named for her regular NTS radio show.

years.src: The Quietus: Laurel Halo Unveils · Wikipedia: Atlas (Laurel Halo album)
years.h: A residency at Ina-GRM in Paris
years.p: She worked on piano sketches at the Paris electroacoustic institute, and the work would become Atlas. Belleville was recorded in a single take in spring 2021.

years.h: Octavia premieres at Maison de la Radio
years.p: Ina-GRM commissioned the multichannel work for piano and electronics, which premiered in Paris and came out in 2024.

eras.title: Atlas
eras.text: A teaching job at CalArts, a move to Los Angeles, and the first record on her own label.

years.h: She joins the faculty at CalArts
years.p: Halo began teaching in the Composition and Experimental Sound Practices program, and moved to Los Angeles in 2023.

years.src: Stereogum: Laurel Halo, Belleville · The Quietus: Laurel Halo Unveils
years.h: "Belleville" comes out with Coby Sey
years.p: The lead single is piano and vibraphone with vocals by Coby Sey.

q: Tracks are never done, you just let them be.
years.src: Wikipedia: Atlas (Laurel Halo album) · Ableton: Laurel Halo, Atlas in the Making · Wikipedia: Laurel Halo
years.h: Atlas: Pitchfork gave it 8.1 and ranked it No. 26 of 2023
years.p: Ten tracks and 40 minutes of piano, strings and vibraphone, with Bendik Giske on sax, Lucy Railton on cello and James Underwood on violin. It is the first release on her own label, Awe.
years.xp:
Piano sketches from Ina-GRM in 2021 were built out in Berlin and London with electronics and acoustic layers. Some collaborators recorded in the room, others sent parts remotely; James Ginzburg mixed and Rashad Becker mastered.

Metacritic has an 80. Pitchfork's review (8.1) called it among her best. Clash gave it 9/10 and ranked it No. 15 of its year. Boomkat named it its album of the year.

years.src: The Quietus: Laurel Halo Unveils · The FADER: Laurel Halo creates
years.h: Atlas live premieres at Berlin Atonal
years.p: Dates followed in Dublin, London, Amsterdam, Bochum and Philadelphia.

eras.title: Octavia, a museum loop and a film
eras.text: She kept writing for spaces and screens rather than returning to songs.

years.h: Octavia is released by GRM
years.p: It came out on Portraits GRM, as a split with Jessica Ekomane's Manifolds.

years.h: Midnight Zone soundtrack
years.p: Her site lists it as an original film score.
